evidence.claim: The executive summary says the most significant issues included extrajudicial killings, torture, arbitrary detention, and forced disappearances by security forces, while civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The executive summary says the most significant issues included extrajudicial killings, torture, arbitrary detention, and forced disappearances by security forces, while civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government country report, mirrored in full text; the summary is explicit and directly relevant to 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Covers calendar year 2022 and was released in 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sheikh Hasina’s government because it describes the state security apparatus under her administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also says civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces, which is a counterweight to the abuse findings.

evidence.claim: The UK report says Bangladesh’s human-rights situation remained a serious concern in 2022, but also notes fewer reports of attacks on people because of religion or belief and a reduction in reports of extrajudicial killings and abductions.
evidence.title: Human Rights and Democracy: the 2022 Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office report
evidence.excerpt: The UK report says Bangladesh’s human-rights situation remained a serious concern in 2022, but also notes fewer reports of attacks on people because of religion or belief and a reduction in reports of extrajudicial killings and abductions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual foreign-policy human-rights report with explicit Bangladesh section and year coverage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment of the Hasina government’s domestic safety environment.
contrary_evidence: The same report emphasizes ongoing harassment, detention, media restrictions, and violence against women and girls, so the positive lines are only partial offsets.

evidence.claim: Freedom House says the 2022 local-election cycle was marred by allegations of fraud and the new Election Commission was selected without opposition participation, reflecting strong perceptions that the commission favored the ruling Awami League.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House says the 2022 local-election cycle was marred by allegations of fraud and the new Election Commission was selected without opposition participation, reflecting strong perceptions that the commission favored the ruling Awami League.
evidence.source_locator: A3 Electoral Laws and Framework; paragraphs on EC selection and 2022 local elections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary country report from a major democracy monitor with explicit 2022 coverage and specific institutional findings.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 politics and preparation for the 2024 national election cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Hasina-era party control over election administration and candidate selection.
contrary_evidence: The same report also notes that independent candidates and defectors defeated AL candidates in some local elections, so competition was not eliminated.

evidence.claim: Freedom House says BNP was able to organize major protests in 2022, though authorities and Awami League supporters disrupted some events, and that independent candidates and defectors defeated AL candidates in the 2021-22 local-election cycle.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House says BNP was able to organize major protests in 2022, though authorities and Awami League supporters disrupted some events, and that independent candidates and defectors defeated AL candidates in the 2021-22 local-election cycle.
evidence.source_locator: B1/B2 paragraphs on opposition protests and local-election cycle
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary country report with explicit 2022 opposition-protest and local-election detail.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 and the immediate pre-election environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina because it describes the government's handling of opposition space and local competition.
contrary_evidence: This is a meaningful counterexample to total closure, because the opposition still managed some large protests and some non-AL candidates won locally.

evidence.claim: The executive summary says Bangladesh's constitution consolidates most power in the Office of the Prime Minister, that the 2018 election was not free and fair, and that 2022 saw serious restrictions on free expression, media, internet freedom, association, judicial independence, and political participation.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The executive summary says Bangladesh's constitution consolidates most power in the Office of the Prime Minister, that the 2018 election was not free and fair, and that 2022 saw serious restrictions on free expression, media, internet freedom, association, judicial independence, and political participation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government country report mirrored in full text.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 and the inherited democratic baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sheikh Hasina's government because it describes the governing structure and state practices under her administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also says civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces, which is a limited counterweight to the abuse findings.

evidence.claim: Freedom House says authorities frequently arrested online critics under the Digital Security Act, increased surveillance capacity, and backed a draft censorship law requiring traceability and long data retention.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House says authorities frequently arrested online critics under the Digital Security Act, increased surveillance capacity, and backed a draft censorship law requiring traceability and long data retention.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary internet-freedom country report with explicit 2022 coverage and specific controls described.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Hasina's government because it concerns state censorship and arrest powers used against critics.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that internet users mobilized online campaigns more actively than in previous years.

evidence.claim: Bachelet said successive UN reports had documented narrowing civic space, increased surveillance, intimidation and reprisals that often led to self-censorship, and she urged stronger independent institutions including the elections commission and judiciary.
evidence.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet concludes her official visit to Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Bachelet said successive UN reports had documented narrowing civic space, increased surveillance, intimidation and reprisals that often led to self-censorship, and she urged stronger independent institutions including the elections commission and judiciary.
evidence.source_locator: Press statement paragraphs on civic space and institutions, lines 70-73 and 103
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN press statement from the High Commissioner's 2022 visit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly on civic space.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level criticism of Hasina's government; not a personal quote, but a direct official assessment of the governing environment.
contrary_evidence: The same statement acknowledges Bangladesh's civil society strength and some women's participation gains, which slightly complicates a one-way decline narrative.

evidence.claim: UN experts said Bangladeshi authorities launched threats, intimidation and harassment against relatives of forcibly disappeared persons and human-rights defenders after U.S. sanctions on RAB officials.
evidence.title: UN experts urge Bangladesh to end reprisals against human rights defenders and relatives of the disappeared
evidence.excerpt: UN experts said Bangladeshi authorities launched threats, intimidation and harassment against relatives of forcibly disappeared persons and human-rights defenders after U.S. sanctions on RAB officials.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the summary of the experts' concerns
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN human-rights press release on a dated 2022 incident pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Hasina's government because the reprisals were alleged against state actors and were triggered by the government's response to sanctions.
contrary_evidence: The statement describes allegations and intimidation patterns, not a formal adjudication of every individual incident.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the authorities were escalating a crackdown on demonstrations, with about 1,400 political activists arrested and more than 60 people injured in the 7 December Dhaka clashes, and called for an end to excessive force and impunity.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Authorities must end repression of demonstrations
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the authorities were escalating a crackdown on demonstrations, with about 1,400 political activists arrested and more than 60 people injured in the 7 December Dhaka clashes, and called for an end to excessive force and impunity.
evidence.source_locator: Background section and the quoted regional director statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization statement tied to a specific 2022 protest crackdown.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Bangladesh authorities under Hasina's government; the report is on state response, not isolated local misconduct.
contrary_evidence: The article relies on media reports for the casualty count, so the exact numbers remain partly contingent.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that since late August 2022 at least four people had died and hundreds had been injured in clashes involving police, BNP supporters, and ruling-party supporters, while police carried out mass arrests of opposition supporters and ruling-party affiliates appeared to enjoy impunity for attacks.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Crackdown on Political Opposition
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that since late August 2022 at least four people had died and hundreds had been injured in clashes involving police, BNP supporters, and ruling-party supporters, while police carried out mass arrests of opposition supporters and ruling-party affiliates appeared to enjoy impunity for attacks.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the Banani candlelight-vigil incident description
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous rights-monitor reporting with specific incident detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because it concerns police conduct and ruling-party-aligned impunity during opposition protests.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that each side accused the other of instigating violence, so not every clash is exclusively state-caused.

evidence.claim: A CGS-linked analysis cited by Prothom Alo said police and ruling-party actors were the plaintiffs or defendants in 47 percent of Digital Security Act cases, and that the law was being used heavily against journalists and critics.
evidence.title: Police-ruling party men are defendants in 47pc DSA cases
evidence.excerpt: A CGS-linked analysis cited by Prothom Alo said police and ruling-party actors were the plaintiffs or defendants in 47 percent of Digital Security Act cases, and that the law was being used heavily against journalists and critics.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the 'Misuse against journalists' section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting that cites a specific research organization and gives concrete case-pattern data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because the DSA was used by police and ruling-party actors against critics and journalists.
contrary_evidence: This is a pattern report, not a court finding on every individual case.

evidence.claim: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration because it said the rights group had published misleading information about extrajudicial killings, disappearances and murders, despite a long-running renewal case.
evidence.title: Govt scraps Odhikar’s registration
evidence.excerpt: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration because it said the rights group had published misleading information about extrajudicial killings, disappearances and murders, despite a long-running renewal case.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and the explanation of the NGO Affairs Bureau letter, lines 198-205 and 213-227
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting with direct documentary detail from the bureau letter.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because the cancellation was carried out by the NGO Affairs Bureau under the Prime Minister's Office.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the cancellation as a paperwork and compliance issue, not purely as retaliation.
